findings.obs_text: The surface meditate carries three codes: H7878 in Psa 77 and Psa 119 and Psa 145:5 (to muse, also to complain), H1897 in Jos 1:8, Psa 63:6, Psa 143:5 and Psa 38:12 (to mutter, also to devise), and H7742 in Gen 24:63 (to muse, its meaning uncertain). In Psa 38:12 the H1897 verb takes treachery as its object.

The surface meditation carries four codes and a preposition: H7881 in Job 15:4, Psa 119:97 and Psa 119:99, H1902H in Psa 19:14, H1900 in Psa 49:3, and H7879 in Psa 104:34, beside H5921A (upon), a small word joined in the unit of Psa 104:34.
findings.grounds: May my meditation be pleasing to him

findings.obs_text: The surface pondering carries two Greek codes: G4820 in Luk 2:19, a verb whose first sense is to throw together, and G1760 in Act 10:19, to revolve in the mind; the English gives one word for both.
The surface ponders carries two codes: H1897 in Pro 15:28, where the heart of the righteous weighs a reply, and H6424 in Pro 5:21, to weigh or make level, said of the Lord and the paths of a man.
